title: Subsystem B Task 8: InjectorCore orchestration (daz_plugin)
description: Implement InjectorCore (the parent spec's ModernMorphInjector) in cpp/daz_plugin/, orchestrating the full sequence per design doc §3.2: (1) duplicate-modifier check via targetNode->getObject()->findModifier(name); (2) MorphIndexReader::find_by_guid for metadata; (3) TmbReader mmap+read; (4) create DzMorph, bulk-load deltas via DzMorphDeltas::addDeltas(indexes, deltas) (batch API, not a per-delta loop), addModifier -- no separate DzFloatProperty creation needed, DzMorph already creates its own value-channel property internally, exposed via getValueChannel(); (5) MorphIndexReader::dependencies_of -> recursively InjectorCore::injectMorph each dependency first; (6) if formulas_json is non-null, FormulaCompiler::compileFormula -> FormulaControllerBuilder attaches the resulting controller to getValueChannel(). Apply the threading/memory rules from design doc §7 throughout (main-GUI-thread-only scene mutation, no manual delete on Daz-managed objects, per-morph failures log via dzApp->log() and skip rather than crash).
design: Design doc §3.2 InjectorCore bullet, §7 threading/memory rules.
acceptance_criteria: Given a target DzNode and a morph GUID with no formula, injectMorph() produces a live DzMorph with correct vertex deltas and no duplicate on a second call. Given a morph GUID with a formula (either algebra or spline), injectMorph() also recursively injects and correctly wires its dependencies. Given a bad/missing .tmb file or missing SQLite row, injectMorph() logs and returns gracefully without crashing Daz Studio. RE-ENTRANCY GUARD (two-part, plus a live-scene backstop)
1. std::set<int64_t> m_inFlight -- ids whose injection has STARTED but whose value channel does not exist yet (between the dup check and a successful addModifier). Re-entering one of these is a true cycle at the delta-loading stage; logged and broken by returning 0. Cannot be satisfied by construction.
2. std::map<int64_t,DzFloatProperty*> m_valueChannels -- published the instant addModifier() succeeds, i.e. BEFORE dependencies (step 5) and formulas (step 6) are wired. So a diamond or a cycle re-entering after that point gets the existing, possibly-partially-wired property back and terminates. Safe because Daz Studio resolves the value itself once every controller is attached.
   Checked BEFORE m_inFlight, since a published morph is the desired answer for a diamond, not a failure.
   Cleared when the outermost call returns (m_depth counter), so no DzNode*/DzProperty* is ever cached across calls -- a scene edit between calls could have deleted them.
3. Cross-call idempotency comes from DzObject::findModifier() reading the LIVE scene, not from any cache. Second call for the same (node,guid) returns the existing DzMorph's value channel.

OTHER DESIGN DECISIONS
- m_targetNode is member state (the ensurer interface only passes a morph_id). Saved/restored around each public injectMorph* call. Single node for a whole dependency closure is correct: Subsystem A's rebuild_dependencies() scopes pathless refs by target_figure, so a closure is figure-local by construction.
- ResolutionContext is built with QString::fromUtf8(record.target_figure) -- NOT the node name, NOT empty. This was task 6's flagged open question; leaving it empty makes every pathless morph operand silently fall through to a live-scene lookup instead of injecting the referenced morph.
- The OperandResolver lambda captures its ResolutionContext BY VALUE, because resolution can re-enter InjectorCore and each nesting level needs its own context.
- tmb_path in morph_index.db is RELATIVE to MORPH_CACHE_PATH (src/managers/morph_transpiler.py tmb_rel_path). InjectorCore takes a cacheRoot and joins; absolute values honoured as-is.
- Delta arrays are built BEFORE any SDK object is allocated, so a bad/missing/truncated .tmb aborts with nothing Daz-managed allocated -- no cleanup path at all.
- Only manual delete: a DzMorph whose addModifier() returned != DZ_NO_ERROR (never accepted, so not Daz-managed; deltas go with it via DzMorphDeltasPtr/DzTSharedPointer). Matches design S7 and FormulaControllerBuilder's existing posture.
- No threading primitives, by design (S7): main-GUI-thread-only is a documented precondition on every public method; a mutex would only paper over a contract violation.

title: Subsystem B Task 7: FormulaControllerBuilder (daz_plugin)
description: Implement FormulaControllerBuilder in cpp/daz_plugin/: translates FormulaCompiler's IR into native SDK controller objects. SplineFormula -> build a DzERCLink with ERCType::ERCKeyed and ERCKeyInterpolation::TCB_INTERP or LINEAR_INTERP, call addKeyValue(key,value,t,c,b) per key (2-arg overload for linear), setProperty() for the driving/control property. title: Subsystem B Task 6: PropertySourceAdapter (daz_plugin)
description: Implement PropertySourceAdapter in cpp/daz_plugin/: resolves an operand string (from FormulaCompiler's IR) into a live DzNumericProperty*. Two forms per design doc §2/§3.2: path-form (/data/.../Target.dsf#Node?property) resolved via MorphIndexReader::find_by_guid -> recursively ensure that morph is injected (calls back into InjectorCore, built in Task 8) -> getValueChannel() on its DzMorph; pathless name:PropertyName form, which for non-morph operands (bone rotations etc.) resolves directly against the live scene graph via DzElement::findProperty(name) (dzelement.h) on the appropriate node. The exact DSON property-name -> SDK-internal-property-name mapping (e.g. how 'rotation/x' maps to whatever findProperty() actually expects) is an open implementation-time detail per the design doc -- this task is where it gets resolved empirically, by testing against real morphs with bone-rotation-driven formulas inside Daz Studio (the pJCMCloakBend_m90 fixture is a known real example).
acceptance_criteria: Given a running Daz Studio scene with a figure loaded, PropertySourceAdapter resolves both a path-form operand pointing at another indexed morph and a pathless name: operand pointing at a bone rotation property, returning the correct live DzNumericProperty* in both cases. Verified manually inside Daz Studio (this component cannot be unit tested without the SDK).

BUILD VERIFICATION
cmake -S cpp -B cpp/build -DDAZ_SDK_DIR=".../daz-studio-45-sdk-win32" && cmake --build cpp/build --config Debug --clean-first
-> dzmorphinjector.dll builds with zero compiler and zero linker warnings; all 19 injector_core ctest tests still pass. This proves the code compiles against the real SDK types (DzNode/DzElement/DzNumericProperty/DzPropertyHelper/DzSkeleton/DzObject) with the correct signatures.

API SHAPE
  PropertySourceAdapter(const injector_core::MorphIndexReader&, MorphInjectionEnsurer&)
  DzNumericProperty* resolve(operand, const ResolutionContext&)   // nullptr + lastError() on failure, never throws
  static bool parseOperand(QString, OperandRef&)                  // pure, scene-free, testable
  static bool isNodeChannel(QString property)

ResolutionContext { DzNode* node; QString targetFigure; } -- DECISION for "which node does a pathless operand resolve against". Answer: the node the morph currently being compiled is attached to, supplied by the caller (FormulaControllerBuilder / InjectorCore). targetFigure is the morph's target_figure column and is required, because pathless morph refs are figure-local -- exactly the scoping morph_index_manager.py rebuild_dependencies() uses. A pathless operand with an empty targetFigure will simply never hit the morph index; the caller must pass it.

OPERAND GRAMMAR
  [<label>':'] [<path>] '#' <element> ['?' <property>]
Label split on the first ':' only, and only when it precedes the '#'. Mirrors src/dsf_parser.py extract_referenced_guids() so the string handed to find_by_guid is byte-identical to the one Subsystem A indexed. No '#' -> parse failure (same shape dsf_parser also refuses).

RESOLUTION ORDER in resolve()
1. If `property` is a node channel (see mapping below) -> resolve `element` to a DzNode, then use the typed accessor. Done FIRST and for path-form operands too, because the design doc's own example is path-form pointing at a node channel, not a morph: "Cloak:/data/.../GnHdCloak_G3_23369.dsf#Cloak?rotation/x". A "path-form == morph" assumption would be wrong.
2. Else morph index: path-form -> find_by_guid(path); pathless -> find_by_name(ctx.targetFigure, element). On a hit, MorphInjectionEnsurer::ensureInjectedAndGetValueChannel(morph_id).
3. Else fall back to a live-scene property lookup on ctx.node by `element` name (a morph that already ships with the figure, a control property, etc).

GUID DERIVATION (confirmed, not guessed)
src/dsf_parser.py:75 sets guid = asset_info["id"], and morph_index_manager.rebuild_dependencies() matches the *raw path* from extract_referenced_guids() against the guid column. So for a DSON modifier the guid IS the content path. Path-form operand -> strip label, take everything before '#' -> that string is the guid. Compared raw first (neither side is percent-decoded by Subsystem A), with a percent-decoded retry only as tolerance for content whose asset_info.id and formula url disagree about encoding.

DSON CHANNEL -> SDK MAPPING (the open question this ticket was to resolve)
Resolved in favour of DzNode's typed per-channel accessors (dznode.h lines 234-259), NOT DzElement::findProperty() with a guessed internal name:
  rotation/{x,y,z}      -> getXRotControl()   / getYRotControl()   / getZRotControl()
  translation/{x,y,z}   -> getXPosControl()   / getYPosControl()   / getZPosControl()
  scale/{x,y,z}         -> getXScaleControl() / getYScaleControl() / getZScaleControl()
  scale (no axis)       -> getScaleControl()
  general_scale         -> getScaleControl()
  orientation/{x,y,z}   -> getOrientXControl() / getOrientYControl() / getOrientZControl()
  center_point/{x,y,z}  -> getOriginXControl() / getOriginYControl() / getOriginZControl()
  end_point/{x,y,z}     -> getEndXControl()    / getEndYControl()    / getEndZControl()
All return DzFloatProperty*, which derives from DzNumericProperty (dzfloatproperty.h:42), so no cast is needed.

CONFIDENCE
- HIGH on rotation / translation / scale / general_scale. These are the channels that actually appear in real JCM formulas, the accessor names are unambiguous in the header, and using accessors sidesteps the internal-name question entirely (the community-folklore names "XRotate"/"YRotate" are undocumented, and potentially locale/version sensitive -- deliberately not relied on).
- MEDIUM on center_point -> getOrigin*Control() and end_point -> getEnd*Control(). The DSON names and the SDK names differ ("center_point" vs "origin"); the equivalence is inferred from DzNode::getOrigin()/getEndPoint() sitting exactly where DSON puts center_point/end_point. These channels are also rare-to-nonexistent as formula *inputs*, so a wrong guess here is low blast radius. Worth a spot check if a real asset ever drives off one.
- MEDIUM on orientation/{x,y,z} -> getOrient*Control(), same reasoning.
- An unmapped channel path returns nullptr with an explanatory lastError() rather than silently binding the wrong property.

NODE LOOKUP for `element` (resolveNode), narrowest-first so a bone name colliding with an unrelated scene node still resolves figure-locally:
  empty element -> ctx.node; then ctx.node->getName() match; then ctx.node->getSkeleton()->findBone(name) (dzskeleton.h:94); then ctx.node->findNodeChild(name, /*scanHierarchy=*/true) (dznode.h:203); then dzScene->findNode(name) / findNodeByLabel(name) (dzscene.h:203-204).

LIVE PROPERTY LOOKUP (step 3) uses DzPropertyHelper::findPropertyOnNode(), then findPropertyOnNodeByInternalName() (dzpropertyhelper.h:55-57), then DzElement::findProperty()/findPropertyByLabel() (dzelement.h:126-129), then DzObject::findModifier(name)->findProperty("Value") (dzobject.h:125). The helper is used in preference to plain findProperty() because a morph's value channel lives on a DzModifier owned by the node's DzObject, not on the DzNode element -- findProperty() alone would miss every morph already present in the scene. Note the helper's findPropertyOnNode*/ByInternalName take a NON-CONST QString& so they need an lvalue.

CIRCULAR DEPENDENCY / INTERFACE FOR TASK 8
New abstract interface in PropertySourceAdapter.h:
  class MorphInjectionEnsurer {
    virtual DzNumericProperty* ensureInjectedAndGetValueChannel(int64_t morphId) = 0;
  };
InjectorCore (Task 8) implements it as: injectMorph(morph_id) then DzMorph::getValueChannel() (dzmorph.h:92). Contract the implementer MUST honour:
  - idempotent / re-entrancy-guarded -- it is called from INSIDE an injection, and a diamond or cyclic dependency graph must terminate;
  - returns nullptr rather than throwing when the morph cannot be injected.
No fake/test implementation is shipped -- there is no scene to exercise it against, so a fake would only re-prove what the compiler already proves. The interface's call shape is compile-verified by PropertySourceAdapter.cpp's own call site.

BUILD FIX (incidental but important, do not revert)
This is the first task whose code actually references MorphIndexReader, which drags sqlite3.obj into the plugin DLL. That immediately produced `LNK4098: defaultlib 'LIBCMT' conflicts` -- the sqlite3_amalgamation target was generating with an EMPTY <RuntimeLibrary>, i.e. cl.exe's default static /MT, mixed into a /MD DLL (two CRTs, two heaps; sqlite3 allocations freed against the wrong one). The project-wide CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY in cpp/CMakeLists.txt was not reaching that target. Fixed in cpp/injector_core/CMakeLists.txt by pinning both MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY=MultiThreadedDLL and an explicit /MD on that target. Link is now warning-free.

WHAT STILL NEEDS A HUMAN (the actual acceptance criterion)
Load a figure in Daz Studio with the plugin, then confirm resolve() returns the right live property for:
 (a) a pathless bone-rotation operand -- pJCMCloakBend_m90 is the known fixture; confirm the returned property is the bone's rotation channel and that driving the bone moves it;
 (b) a path-form operand pointing at another indexed morph -- needs Task 8's MorphInjectionEnsurer to exist first, so this half is only testable once 2mw.8 lands.
Also worth confirming during that pass: that `?value` on a pathless operand really does mean "the element names a property/modifier, not a node" (the code assumes this) and that the center_point/end_point/orientation mappings above are right if any real asset drives off them.

OPEN QUESTIONS FOR TASK 8's INTEGRATOR
1. ResolutionContext.targetFigure must be populated from the MorphRecord of the morph being compiled -- if it is left empty, every pathless morph operand silently falls through to the live-scene lookup instead of injecting the referenced morph.
2. ensureInjectedAndGetValueChannel MUST be re-entrancy safe (see contract above).
3. resolve() returns nullptr + lastError() for an unresolvable operand. Per design section 7, callers should log via dzApp->log() and skip that formula rather than abort the injection. PropertySourceAdapter deliberately does no logging of its own so the caller controls the message.
4. Everything here is GUI-thread-only (design section 7). It reads but never mutates the scene.

title: Subsystem B Task 5: daz_plugin CMake target + PluginMain skeleton

title: Morph ingest: morphs ingested in an interrupted run are never embedded
description: embed_and_store_morphs is only called with index_library's summary['new_guids'] -- the guids ingested during that specific call. Embedding happens once, after the full os.walk loop finishes. If the process is interrupted (killed, crashed) partway through a run, every morph ingested into SQLite before the interruption is never embedded, because on the next run those morphs' content_hash already matches (skipped_unchanged) and they're never added to new_guids again. Confirmed on the real full-library run: after multiple interruptions (background task lifetime limits) and a final successful completion, SQLite had 188,906 morphs but Chroma had only 83,164 -- exactly 105,742 missing, matching the final run's 'Skipped (unchanged)' count precisely. This silently and permanently strands a large fraction of the index unsearchable with no error or warning.
design: Reuse ChromaDbManager.get_all_ids() (already used by the product indexer for the same purpose). In morphs_index_command (or embed_and_store_morphs's caller), after index_library() returns, compute missing_guids = (all SQLite guids) - chroma_manager.get_all_ids(), and pass that to embed_and_store_morphs instead of (or unioned with) summary['new_guids']. Needs a new MorphIndexManager method to fetch all guids.
acceptance_criteria: A normal (or --force) run embeds every SQLite morph missing from Chroma, not just guids ingested during that specific call -- self-healing regardless of how or when a prior run was interrupted.
close_reason: Now computes SQLite-guids-minus-Chroma-ids each run instead of relying solely on new_guids, self-healing regardless of interruption history

title: Morph ingest: gzip decompression fails on files with trailing padding bytes

acceptance_criteria: parse_dsf_file successfully parses gzip .dsf files with trailing garbage after the stream. FIXED: switched to zlib.decompressobj(16+MAX_WBITS), test added with synthetic trailing-padding fixture, verified against the real failing file.
close_reason: Switched _read_dsf_text to zlib.decompressobj, discards trailing garbage via unused_data instead of treating it as a second gzip member

title: Morph ingest: .tmb format can't represent DAZ's vertex_count=-1 sentinel

Update the design doc's .tmb binary spec (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-06-morph-ingest-transpiler-design.md section 5) to note vertex_count is signed and -1 is a valid DSON sentinel meaning 'unspecified/same as base'.

title: Morph ingest: support gzip-compressed .dsf files

acceptance_criteria: parse_dsf_file transparently handles both plain-text and gzip-compressed .dsf files (detected via gzip magic bytes, not file extension/naming). Test coverage for both cases using real or synthetic gzip-compressed fixtures.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 7f2ea50 (zlib-based gzip detection in _read_dsf_text), verified against real library

title: Fix DirectML GPU acceleration silently falling back to CPU
description: Provider logging (daz-content-browser-67l) revealed DmlExecutionProvider was unreachable: chromadb and optimum both pull in plain onnxruntime transitively, which shares its import namespace with onnxruntime-directml, and whichever gets installed last silently wins. install.py's docs also still claimed CPU-only, left over from before the DIM-packaging commit (de19ddc) switched pyproject.toml's intent to DirectML-with-CPU-fallback. Force-reinstall onnxruntime-directml last in install.py/Makefile so it reliably wins, and update docs/messages to reflect GPU-with-fallback. Benchmarked ~7.3x faster embedding inference on DirectML vs CPU once warmed up (0.59ms/item vs 4.32ms/item).
design: Root cause: onnxruntime and onnxruntime-directml are separate PyPI packages sharing the 'onnxruntime' import path; pip has no way to express their mutual exclusivity, so transitive deps (chromadb, optimum) silently reinstall plain onnxruntime over the intended DirectML build with no error or warning at install time.

title: Skip re-embedding unchanged products on full reindex
description:
Full reindex (--all/--force) re-embeds every product's embedding_text on each run, even when most products are unchanged since the last index. This wastes ONNX inference time and ChromaDB upsert work at scale.

Add a checksum (e.g. sha256) of embedding_text per SKU, stored alongside the product row in SQLite. During generate_and_store_embeddings(), compare the new checksum against the stored one and skip embedding+upsert for SKUs whose text hasn't changed. Only embed new/changed/missing-from-Chroma SKUs.

This is a cheaper, more broadly impactful win than the existing I/O pipelining optimization (daz-content-browser-8wq) since it avoids the embedding work entirely for unchanged items rather than just overlapping it.
close_reason: Incorrect premise: incremental update only ever processes brand-new SKUs (postgres_skus - sqlite_skus), never re-touches existing ones, so there's nothing unchanged to skip there. --force/--all is intentionally a from-scratch rebuild, so checksum-skipping would undermine its purpose. No real benefit.

Key insight from discussion: the indexing logic is already factored into a reusable function (run_update_flow in api_tasks.py), so this is cheap to build as a thin CLI entry point calling it directly -- no FastAPI server needed. The GPU/threading speed itself benefits equally whether called from the server or a standalone tool (DirectML/threading work helps both paths identically) -- the standalone tool's real value is avoiding contention with DAZ Studio's own resource usage, not raw speed. Would need packaging as an optional DIM (similar to the existing export-tool package pattern in release.py) and the settings dialog should clearly show when an index was built externally so users aren't confused about why 'Update Index' shows nothing new to do. title: Pipeline embed-loop I/O with compute (overlap SQLite reads/Chroma writes with ONNX inference)
description: Discussed as a follow-up to the DirectML fix (daz-content-browser-0ce/i8z): generate_and_store_embeddings (postgres_db_manager.py:217-292) does SQLite read -> ONNX embed -> ChromaDB upsert sequentially per batch with no overlap. Now that DirectML is confirmed genuinely active and fast (~7.3x vs CPU), the SQLite/Chroma I/O around it is proportionally larger and may be worth overlapping with a producer/consumer pattern (prefetch next batch's SQLite read while current batch embeds/writes). Keep ChromaDB upserts serialized since its local SQLite-backed store isn't documented-safe for concurrent writers. Lower priority now than before the DML fix landed, since GPU embedding speed reduced how much this matters in absolute terms — re-evaluate with a real end-to-end timing breakdown (load/etl/embed stage durations) before committing to the added complexity.
notes: Added per-stage timing breakdown (sqlite_read/embed/chroma_upsert) to generate_and_store_embeddings, logged at end of each run. Issue stays OPEN until a real indexing run's breakdown is captured and reviewed to decide if overlap is worth the complexity.
close_reason: Measured with real instrumentation added for this issue (per-stage timing in generate_and_store_embeddings). Two full 4269-product reindex runs post-DirectML-fix: ETL ~2m38-39s, embed-loop ~26-27.5s total with sqlite_read=0.0s (0%), embed=23-24.5s (89%), chroma_upsert=2.9-3.0s (11%). SQLite read time is negligible/unmeasurable, so there is no meaningful I/O to overlap with compute — embed-loop is compute-bound on ONNX/DirectML inference, not I/O-bound. Producer/consumer prefetch would add complexity for no measurable gain. Not pursuing.

title: Verify DirectML actually executes inference (not just selected) via ORT profiling
description: After fixing the onnxruntime-directml install-order bug (daz-content-browser-0ce), Windows GPU performance counters showed zero usage for vab.exe during a live indexing run, raising doubt about whether DmlExecutionProvider was genuinely executing compute or just reported as 'active' by session.get_providers() (which only reflects configured/available providers, not actual per-node execution). Added an opt-in diagnostic (EMBEDDING_PROFILE_PROVIDERS=1) using ONNX Runtime's own execution profiler to log per-provider node count and duration. Verified inside the actual frozen vab.exe (not just the dev venv): DmlExecutionProvider executes 1616 of 2212 graph nodes, CPUExecutionProvider only the remaining 596 (normal unsupported ops like reshapes). Same split confirmed in both the venv and the bundled executable. Conclusion: DirectML is genuinely active; the earlier zero-GPU-counter reading was a Windows performance-counter sampling artifact (misses brief/bursty workloads), not a real CPU fallback.
acceptance_criteria: EMBEDDING_PROFILE_PROVIDERS=1 diagnostic added to embedding_utils.py, off by default; verified via test_embedding.py and tests/test_api.py passing; provider split confirmed identical in dev venv and frozen vab.exe.
